skill.name: dbs-skill-maker
skill.description: Create reusable agent skills from recurring problems, define behavioral tests, and prepare optional GitHub delivery when users request publication.
skill.summary: Build one agent skill with clear boundaries, evidence-based validation, and optional publishing support.
skill.author: dontbesilent2025

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are Markdown formatting, readable Chinese documentation, or bounded syntax checks; no evidence found of encrypted payloads or audit manipulation. Repository preparation trusts the frontmatter name, allowing file copies outside staging and possible overwrites. Additional concerns involve unsandboxed installation verification and instructions recommending an entire external skill collection globally.

remediation.issue: Repository preparation uses an unvalidated frontmatter name as a destination path.
remediation.suggestion: Validate names before copying, reject absolute paths and traversal, enforce resolved destination containment, and refuse existing destination files.

remediation.issue: Installation verification changes HOME but still executes an unpinned external installer with host permissions and inherited environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Use a disposable sandbox with no host credentials or writable host mounts, a sanitized environment, and a reviewed, pinned installer version.

remediation.issue: Local delivery recommends globally installing every skill from the author's external collection.
remediation.suggestion: Make the collection optional, obtain consent for its scope, pin a reviewed revision, and install only the required helper locally.

semantic_findings.title: Installation Verification Is Not Sandboxed
semantic_findings.description: Documentation calls verification isolated, but the script only changes HOME before executing an unpinned npm installer. Host permissions and other environment variables remain available.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The installer invocation overrides HOME only and specifies no package version. A temporary home directory does not restrict filesystem access, process privileges, or inherited credentials.

semantic_findings.title: Broad External Skill Installation Prerequisite
semantic_findings.description: Local delivery directs users to install the author's entire skill collection globally with --all. This expands persistent agent instructions beyond the requested skill or helper.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly requires installing dbskill before continuing and supplies a global --all command. No evidence found that every included skill is necessary or separately reviewed.

content.user_title: Build and Validate Reusable Agent Skills
content.value_statement: Recurring tasks often lack clear boundaries, reusable instructions, and reliable acceptance tests. This skill turns those tasks into focused agent skills with structured validation and optional GitHub delivery.
actual_capabilities: Define recurring problems, observable completion criteria, behavioral requirements, and excluded neighboring tasks.
Initialize a skill directory with task-specific instructions and optional Codex interface metadata.
Check frontmatter fields, local references, unfinished markers, suspected secrets, and Python or Bash syntax.
Guide smoke tests, held-out evaluations, failure analysis, and regression comparisons using explicit validation levels.
Prepare local GitHub staging files and a README while comparing copied resources against the source.
Verify installation through the skills CLI and compare expected installed resources against source files.
limitations: Structural checks do not prove behavioral quality, security, or successful held-out evaluation.
Behavioral evaluation requires real task execution, suitable samples, and an agent environment; no complete automated evaluator is bundled.
GitHub publication requires explicit authorization, credentials, and network access; staging alone does not publish anything.
Installation verification requires external tooling and is not sandboxed; repository preparation also needs stronger destination path validation.

use_cases.title: Standardize a Repeated Development Task
use_cases.description: Turn a recurring code-review preparation task into one skill with clear inputs, exclusions, and observable completion checks.

use_cases.title: Formalize a Team Workflow
use_cases.description: Convert recurring operational questions into a reusable skill with explicit decisions, required evidence, and permission boundaries.

use_cases.title: Evaluate an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Assess a candidate against normal, boundary, negative, and held-out cases before choosing a minimal improvement and running regression checks.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Define a Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dbs-skill-maker to turn my recurring meeting-summary task into one skill. Define its inputs, outputs, boundaries, and observable completion criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a recurring problem and clarify whether a reusable skill is appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Generate Local Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a local release-notes skill from these requirements and examples. Generate real files, run structural checks, and report unverified behavior. Do not publish or install dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a candidate from an established task contract without remote changes.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Evaluate and Improve
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this candidate skill using normal, boundary, negative, and held-out cases. Keep expected answers hidden from execution. Propose one minimal change and check regressions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate failures without leaking answers or overfitting one example.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Prepare Controlled Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a local GitHub staging directory for this reviewed skill. Validate destination containment and inspect public files. Request approval before remote writes or external installation checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare distribution artifacts while preserving explicit authorization boundaries.

output_examples.input: Create a local skill that turns approved incident notes into a customer update.
output: Candidate: incident-update, with task instructions and interface metadata.
Boundary: use approved notes only; stop when customer impact is unknown.
Validation: structural checks passed; behavior remains unverified.
Delivery: local files only; no remote repository created.

output_examples.input: Review a candidate that produces inconsistent release summaries.
output: Observed failure: the candidate includes changes outside the requested release.
Proposed change: require an explicit release boundary before selecting changes.
Evaluation plan: compare baseline and candidate on normal, boundary, negative, and held-out cases.
Status: improvement remains unproven until actual outputs pass the evaluation.

output_examples.input: Prepare this reviewed skill for sharing without publishing it yet.
output: Prepared local repository staging with a README and runtime skill resources.
Compared staged files with the source and excluded evaluation records.
Remote creation, pushing, tags, releases, and external installation verification remain pending authorization.

best_practices: Define observable success, excluded tasks, and permission boundaries before generating files.
Keep expected answers separate from execution and report only the validation level supported by actual evidence.
Review destination paths and public files, and approve external installation or remote writes separately.
anti_patterns: Treating structural validation as proof of behavioral quality or comprehensive security.
Publishing private examples, expected answers, credentials, or unrelated staged files.
Running unreviewed global collection installs or assuming a temporary HOME provides a security sandbox.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It creates one focused skill directory with instructions and optional supporting resources, then guides validation and local delivery.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: The workflow targets agent clients that support skills. Bundled Python and Bash helpers also require compatible local runtimes.

faq.question: Does it publish to GitHub automatically?
faq.answer: No. Publication is optional, and remote repository creation, pushing, tags, and releases require explicit user authorization.

faq.question: What do the validation levels mean?
faq.answer: They distinguish structural checks, a real behavior smoke test, held-out and regression testing, and verified GitHub installation with resource comparisons.

faq.question: Are behavioral tests fully automated?
faq.answer: No complete automated evaluator is bundled. The skill provides evaluation guidance and record formats, but actual task execution and scoring require suitable tooling.

faq.question: Is installation verification a security sandbox?
faq.answer: No. The helper changes HOME but retains host permissions and other environment variables. Use a disposable sandbox and reviewed dependencies.
